storylines.label: Deep Research
storylines.latest_title: DRFLOW: A Deep Research Benchmark for Personalized Workflow Prediction

prior_narrative.tldr: In mid-June, deep research agents got pushed on both evaluation and engineering. An arXiv paper argued that existing benchmarks only grade a single-shot report and miss whether an agent improves when given feedback, and ran a multi-turn evaluation under process-level feedback. AWS then shipped a concrete build pattern: an end-to-end competitive research agent on Deep Agents and Bedrock AgentCore with isolated execution for multi-step workflows. The latest beat, DRFLOW, reframes the target again, arguing real enterprise work needs the agent to predict a personalized workflow rather than just produce a report, and proposing a benchmark for it.
prior_narrative.whats_new: The newest item, DRFLOW (Jun 16), moves the benchmark goalposts past report generation toward predicting personalized, enterprise-style workflows — a different success criterion than the feedback-driven report quality the Jun 8 paper measured.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: How you evaluate a deep research agent is still unsettled: single-shot report quality, improvement under process-level feedback, and personalized workflow prediction are three different bars, and the one you pick changes what you build. AWS's Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore walkthrough is a ready reference for the isolated-execution, multi-step plumbing underneath any of them.

storylines.label: Fable Mythos
storylines.latest_title: Anthropic Releases and Temporarily Suspends Claude Fable 5

prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the higher Mythos 5 tier in mid-June, billing the Mythos-class model as made safe for general use, though launch coverage immediately flagged controversial usage terms; an early hands-on found Fable 5 "relentlessly proactive." Then on Jun 13 the story turned: a US government export-control directive, citing national security, suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and industry coverage reframed the launch as models deemed too dangerous to release. A later recap framed the takedown as a temporary suspension.
prior_narrative.whats_new: An outside recap from InfoQ is the first to characterize the takedown as a temporary suspension — tying it to a US export-control directive — rather than a permanent pull.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A top-tier model can go from general-availability launch to government-ordered suspension within days, and even a 'temporary' status leaves re-enablement uncertain.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," then a US export-control directive pulled access on national-security grounds. Latest framing: the takedown is a temporary suspension, not a permanent pull.

open_questions: Is "temporary" confirmed — does any re-enable date appear?
Does the export-control directive extend to other frontier labs?
How are downstream products handling the sudden loss of access?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: A flagship can go GA → government-suspended in days. Keep a fallback model wired in rather than hard-coding a single flagship tier into production.
